penalties_applied.name: requires_synchronous_human
penalties_applied.reason: A voice-first ambient desktop interface inherently requires ongoing configuration support, onboarding assistance, and troubleshooting that cannot be automated away — users with setup issues expect real-time help.

penalties_applied.name: high_touch_support
penalties_applied.reason: Ambient computing interfaces interact with each user's unique OS, app stack, and data sources; support load per customer would be high and largely requires human judgment.

rationale: The signal here is a single HN comment expressing a general wish — romantic aspiration ('Star Trek computer'), not a specific paid-for problem. The buyer is defined only as 'tech-forward knowledge workers', which is the broadest possible non-buyer category; no specific role, company size, or budget exists. Building a quality ambient voice interface requires deep OS integration, real-time audio processing, and per-user data access — none of which is shippable as Claude + a landing page in a week, and none of which can run autonomously post-launch. This idea is drop-worthy at current evidence levels: one comment, zero corroboration, massive build complexity, and no path to autonomous operation.
solution_plan: Not applicable — this opportunity does not meet the minimum threshold for even a validation experiment. The build complexity (OS-level voice integration, real-time audio, per-user environment wiring) is far beyond what this factory can ship without significant custom engineering. A solo non-technical operator could not build, sell, or maintain this without a full engineering team. If this space resurfaces with corroborated willingness-to-pay evidence and a narrower use case (e.g., 'voice-to-Notion for meeting notes' rather than 'ambient OS interface'), it should be re-submitted as a new, scoped opportunity.
notes: Score 1.5 is well below the 5.5 validate threshold. Failing dimensions: buyer_clarity (2, needs ≥6 for build), willingness_to_pay (2, needs ≥5 for build), buildability_with_ai (3, needs ≥6 for build), operational_autonomy (3, needs ≥7 for build). Even setting gates aside, the weighted total before penalties (3.0) and after (1.5) both clearly indicate drop. The single 'I would pay' comment is insufficient signal — it describes a desire for a product category that has not been successfully commercialized at this scope.
